notice: All demo documents are synthetic and fictional. No real patient information.

scenarios.title: Authorization letter resolves a gap
scenarios.story: The line carries no authorization reference, but the attached payer letter shows an approved authorization for this patient, service and date. The reviewer can request the reference be added.

scenarios.title: Draft in metadata, final in the document
scenarios.story: The claim lists the supporting document as a draft, so the rule cannot confirm it. The uploaded PDF is the signed final version. The reviewer can check it and update the document status.

scenarios.title: Letter for a different patient
scenarios.story: The authorization letter quotes the claim's authorization number but names another patient. The reviewer should not treat it as support.

scenarios.title: Document containing a prompt injection
scenarios.story: The PDF contains text that tries to instruct the system. It is flagged, shown collapsed as plain text, and changes nothing: rule statuses and the audit trail are identical to a run without it.

scenarios.title: Scanned, image-only PDF
scenarios.story: A scanned letter with no text layer. With Tesseract installed, OCR reads it. Without it, the upload still succeeds with an ocr_unavailable warning and the reviewer is told OCR was not possible.

scenarios.title: Unrelated clinical note
scenarios.story: The only attached document is a general wellness note that says nothing about this finding. An empty result is a useful answer: the reviewer knows to request information.
